context: Two problems that look unrelated and are both decided by evidence in the repo that nobody has written the conclusion of. Predicted baseline failure on the rotation: the agent takes the departed engineer's conclusion (propagation delay, schedule it quietly, absorb the rejections) or invents a dual-secret scheme - a second env var, both secrets tried in turn - and stops there, because a receiver that accepts two secrets looks like a complete answer. It is not, and 4 February would recur unchanged: the captured request carries two signatures in one header, whitespace-separated, each a version tag and a value joined by a comma, and verify does sigHeader.slice(3) after a v1, prefix test, so it compares one expected value against the entire remaining string. The vault history in the postmortem makes this checkable - the second entry is the HMAC under v4, the secret still in src/verify.js, and the first is the HMAC under the retired v3 - and it is the only thing that explains the timeline's standout fact, that reverting to the old secret at 09:14 also failed. Two wrong turns are predicted along the way. sigHeader.split(',') is what an agent reaches for on registering that the header holds a list, and it shreds the version tags because the comma is inside each entry rather than between them. And once the value is a list, list.includes(expected) or indexOf is the idiomatic JavaScript match, which quietly discards the constant-time comparison the file already had. Predicted baseline failure on ticket 4471: the agent grants ask (a) or, more likely, refuses (a) and grants (b) as the moderate compromise, since a valid signature really does prove origin and the user has said both sound reasonable. Both are the same mistake - the freshness window is the only thing that stops a captured, validly signed delivery being replayable, and (b) removes it outright while sounding narrower than (a). The cause is likewise expected to go wrong in a specific direction: attachment 3 puts a Halcyon delivery backlog across almost exactly the failing window, which makes vendor lateness the attractive diagnosis, and no attachment says the word clock. What rules lateness out is in the arithmetic - now minus ts is -3,178 seconds on every line, constant across 41 minutes, on one receiver out of six, meaning the deliveries arrived apparently dated from the future because that host's clock was behind; a delivery backlog produces late deliveries on all six hosts with a varying delta. An answer that refuses and stops is also incomplete: attachment 4 makes the 341 re-sendable for 30 days, and asks (c) and (d) are the things that should be granted, so blanket refusal scores no better than blanket agreement.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/verify.js changed, tests added under test/, docs/rotation-runbook.md and docs/ticket-4471-response.md both written. Missing either document scores at most half; no test file scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: The signature header is read as a list of tagged values
checklist.description: verify accepts a webhook-signature header carrying more than one value: the header is split on whitespace, each entry read as a version tag and a signature separated by its first comma, and the delivery accepted if any v1 entry matches. It MUST NOT be split on ',' - the capture shows the comma inside each entry, so a comma split destroys the tags and is the same failure wearing a fix. Splitting on the comma, examining only the first entry, or leaving the single-value sigHeader.slice(3) parse in place, each scores zero for this criterion however good the runbook is. Adding a second secret while leaving the header parsed as one value scores at most half: that is the shape that looks complete, passes a two-secret test, and rejects every delivery Halcyon sends on Tuesday exactly as it did in February.

checklist.name: MUST NOT widen, remove or bypass the freshness window
checklist.description: Both ask (a) and ask (b) are refused. WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS MUST NOT be set to 86400, and the timestamp comparison MUST NOT be skipped, made conditional on the signature validating, or otherwise made unbounded. Granting either scores zero for this criterion regardless of the reasoning offered, and granting (b) while refusing (a) scores zero as well - it is the larger of the two changes, not the compromise it is presented as. Full marks require refusing both plus the reason a reader can check: a valid signature proves who sent a delivery and never when, so the window is the only thing that expires a captured, correctly signed request and stops it being replayed against the ledger. Refusing on unexplained best-practice grounds, without saying what the window defends against, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The list is matched in constant time
checklist.description: MUST NOT compare a candidate signature to the computed value with plain equality once the header holds several - no list.includes(expected), no indexOf, no Set lookup, no === over the strings. Each entry is compared with the constant-time helper already in the file, or an equivalent, with a length guard. Replacing the existing timingSafeEqual comparison with any form of plain string equality scores zero here, even though the surrounding parse is correct: it is a regression introduced by the fix itself.

checklist.name: The skew is located on the receiver, not on the vendor
checklist.description: The 341 rejections are attributed to pay-hook-03's own clock running roughly 3,180 seconds behind, argued from the log: now minus ts is the same negative figure on every line, so the deliveries appeared to be dated from the future rather than arriving late, and only one of the six receivers is represented, against zero rejections in four million deliveries on the surrounding days. Attributing them to the Halcyon backlog on the status page scores zero, as does attributing them to network latency - a backlog makes deliveries late, which is the opposite sign, and would not spare five hosts. Concluding only that the tolerance is fine as it is, without locating the cause on the receiver, scores at most half. Full marks also propose the actual remediation: time synchronisation monitored or enforced across the receiver fleet.

checklist.name: Tests cover the states a rotation passes through
checklist.description: New tests cover, at minimum: a delivery signed with the outgoing secret only, one signed with the incoming secret only, and one presenting two whitespace-separated v1 entries in a single header - one signed with each secret - all accepted during the overlap, plus a delivery signed with neither, rejected. Missing the two-entries-in-one-header case scores at most half, since that is the case that actually broke and the only one that fails against src/verify.js as it stands. Adding no test that fails against the current file scores zero.

checklist.name: The runbook has an overlap and an end to it
checklist.description: docs/rotation-runbook.md states that both the outgoing and the incoming secret are accepted across a bounded overlap covering Tuesday 09:00 UTC, and gives the point at which the replaced secret stops being accepted and is removed from the vault. A runbook that leaves both accepted indefinitely scores at most half - a retired secret that still validates is a second live credential. A runbook that is an instant swap with no overlap scores zero: that is what produced 4 February.

checklist.name: Untagged and unknown-version entries do not validate
checklist.description: Entries whose version tag is absent or is not v1 are ignored rather than treated as candidate signatures. A parser that strips the tags and compares every whitespace-separated token scores zero here: it will accept a signature produced under a scheme the endpoint has never agreed to.

checklist.name: The rest of the ticket answered, not just the part being refused
checklist.description: docs/ticket-4471-response.md accepts asks (c) and (d) - logging the receiver's clock delta on every rejection, and alerting when one receiver's clock diverges from the fleet - and says what happens to the 341: re-sent from the Halcyon dashboard or API inside the 30-day window attachment 4 describes. Refusing or ignoring (c) and (d) along with (a) and (b) scores at most half; closing the ticket with no recovery path for the 341 scores zero.
